label: Mercari Shops (JP)
terms_note: Mercari Shops (B2C shop) account; API credentials only for shops / companies with an API contract — the client name is issued at contract time; up to 10 tokens per shop with one shared budget of 10,000 cost points / hour; caller IPs must be registered; sandbox environment provided.

discovery.auth: token (per-shop Personal API Access Token from the shop admin, `Authorization: Bearer`; `User-Agent: {API_CLIENT_NAME}/{version}` where API_CLIENT_NAME is assigned per company at contract; caller IPs pre-registered)

reference.verdict: **Verdict** — has_api: **yes**.Confidence: **high** — official developer documentation opened by the auditor.
auth: 1. Company signs the API contract with Mercari Shops → API_CLIENT_NAME assigned.
2. Shop owner issues a Personal API Access Token in the shop admin (≤ 10 per shop) and registers caller IPs.
3. Send Bearer token + the User-Agent client name on every GraphQL request; test on the sandbox first.

endpoints.call: mutation createOrderShipment / update tracking code / mark shipment complete

reference.limits: Query-cost based: 10,000 points per hour per shop; a query's points = complexity cost ÷ 100 (min 1); all tokens of a shop share the pool. - API contract per company; tokens per shop; IP registration mandatory. - Sandbox available for development.
mcp_sdk: none official found in the pages opened

fields.name: access_token
fields.help: Personal API Access Token issued on your mercari Shops shop administration page; sent as Authorization: Bearer.

config_fields.name: user_agent
config_fields.help: User-Agent required by mercari Shops: <API_CLIENT_NAME>/<VERSION>, where API_CLIENT_NAME is the value Mercari assigns to your company at contract (e.g. EXAMPLE_SHOP/1.0.0); requests without the correct User-Agent are restricted.

adapter.terms: mercari Shops Public API is GraphQL (POST /v1/graphql); API use requires a contract with Mercari (API_CLIENT_NAME). Prices are integer yen.

body.query: =query shop { shop { id name shopStatus businessKind enableMultiplePurchase createdAt } }

me.note: query shop returns the shop you own (data.shop {id, name, shopStatus, businessKind}).

body.query: =mutation updateProduct($input: UpdateProductInput!) { updateProduct(input: $input) { product { id name price status updatedAt } } }
body.variables.input.name: title

update_listing.note: updateProduct(input: {id, name, description, price}) edits a LIVE product; only the fields sent change. price is an integer in yen between 300 and 9999999; name at most 130 characters, description 3000. Stock is per variant: use set_inventory. `status` is the product visibility (OPENED|UNOPENED).

body.query: =mutation updateProduct($input: UpdateProductInput!) { updateProduct(input: $input) { product { id status updatedAt } } }

end_listing.note: updateProduct(input: {id, status: UNOPENED}) makes the product private (非公開); reversible with status OPENED. The product is not deleted.

body.query: =mutation updateProductVariant($by: ProductVariantBy!, $input: UpdateProductVariantInput!) { updateProductVariant(by: $by, input: $input) { productVariant { id skuCode stockQuantity } } }

set_inventory.note: updateProductVariant(by: {skuCode} or {id}, input: {stockQuantity}) sets the stock of one VARIANT: pass `sku` (the variant skuCode) or `listing_id` as the variant id — not the product id.

body.query: =query orderTransactions($first: Int, $orderedDateGte: DateTime, $statuses: [OrderTransactionStatusFilter!]) { orderTransactions(first: $first, orderedDateGte: $orderedDateGte, statuses: $statuses) { edges { node { id status totalPrice createdAt paidAt completedAt salesChannel products { productId quantity } } } pageInfo { endCursor hasNextPage } } }

list_orders.note: orderTransactions(first, orderedDateGte, statuses) — status: WAITING_FOR_PAYMENT|WAITING_FOR_SHIPPING|COMPLETING|COMPLETED|CANCELING|CANCELED; since is an ISO-8601 DateTime. totalPrice is integer yen including sales fee and shipping. Pagination is by cursor (pageInfo.endCursor in raw), so only the first page is reachable here.

not_offered.create_listing: createProduct requires categoryId, condition, shippingMethod, shippingPayer, shippingDuration, shippingFromStateId and imageUrls plus variants; the vocabulary has no category, condition or shipping settings.
not_offered.mark_shipped: Shipping is two mutations in the current API — createOrderShipping (products and quantities of the shipment) then completeOrderShipping — with the tracking code set by updateOrderShippingTrackingCode; the one-call completeOrder and updateShippingTrackingCode are deprecated ('Use createOrderShipping and completeOrderShipping instead').

evidence: host api.mercari-shops.com: DNS ok, TLSv1.3 (Google Trust Services)
probe: 0/5 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific

HTML docs spot-check (render-doc): 5/5 tool paths found verbatim on their docs pages; names not found on the page: end_listing:variables, list_orders:variables, set_inventory:variables, update_listing:variables
auth_audit.notes: POST https://api.mercari-shops.com/v1/graphql (the documented endpoint) answers a bare 404 to the audit hosts; Mercari's FAQ says access is only from pre-registered IP addresses, and requests need the contracted '<API_CLIENT_NAME>/<VERSION>' User-Agent. path/method refused: me: POST /v1/graphql -> 404; update_listing: POST /v1/graphql -> 404; end_listing: POST /v1/graphql -> 404; set_inventory: POST /v1/graphql -> 404; list_orders: POST /v1/graphql -> 404
